problem: Instruction-following navigation in dynamic environments requires satisfying multiple simultaneous specifications (e.g. overtake a pedestrian while staying on the right), and the number of combinations grows exponentially. Existing VLM-policy baselines (CoNVOI, VLM-Social-Nav) are slow and inconsistent, and costmap-composition (BehAV) gets stuck in local minima, so all degrade quickly as specifications increase.
motivation: Users want to customize robot behavior around humans (yield, follow, overtake, avoid regions), but training one model per specification combination is impractical. Composing independently learned motion primitives cuts the cost from exponential to linear, and diffusion models can be composed as products of distributions. Per-primitive demonstrations are costly, whereas verifying a trajectory with a rule or VLM is easy, which motivates RL fine-tuning.
key_idea: Learn each navigation motion primitive as a diffusion model (supervised pre-training on generic collision-free trajectories, then per-primitive RL fine-tuning with DDPO), and compose them at test time by summing classifier-free-guidance noise predictions to satisfy unseen combinations of specifications.
insight: RL fine-tuning of a generic pretrained planner turns it into near-perfect primitives without primitive-specific demos: pre-trained SR is 27-48% on L/R/F/Y/W versus 99-100% after fine-tuning. Composing the primitives at test time generalizes to unseen combinations and degrades much more slowly than VLM-policy or costmap baselines (34.9% vs <11% at four specifications). Accuracy still declines with more specifications, which the authors attribute to naive noise-sum composition.
method: Problem formulation: an instruction decomposes into independent binary specifications φ(τ,O); a trajectory follows the instruction iff it satisfies all of them. Specifications and observations are assumed to come from an upstream LLM/VLM.

Supervised pre-training: a base conditional diffusion model (1D UNet with a transformer context encoder over object-centric observations) is trained on ~2M synthetic time-dependent collision-free trajectories from RRT plus spatio-temporal Hybrid A* with varied planner hyperparameters; 25 denoising steps.

RL fine-tuning (DDPO/PPO): the base model is fine-tuned separately for each of six primitives (pass left, pass right, follow, yield, walk through region, avoid region) in random simulated environments with rule-based binary rewards (lr 1e-6, 1000 epochs, 32 envs/epoch).

Composition at deployment: p(τ|specs) ∝ p(τ)∏p(τ|φi,oi)/p(τ) realized via classifier-free guidance. The composed noise is the average unconditional prediction plus the sum of w_i(cond − uncond), with w_i=1, and it drives the standard reverse diffusion process.

Real-time execution: MPPI controller tracks the time-dependent waypoints at 10 Hz. Replanning perturbs the previous trajectory with 5 forward and 5 reverse diffusion steps, with vmap batching across primitives and torch.compile.
Robot system: a Jackal with a ZED 2i for human tracking and an Ouster LiDAR, running onboard on an i7 CPU and an RTX A2000.

setting.backbone: Per-primitive 1D-UNet diffusion planners with a transformer context encoder (pretrained then RL fine-tuned) + MPPI controller; the upstream LLM/VLM is abstracted away
setting.training_data: ~2M synthetic collision-free trajectories (pretraining, including region avoid/traverse labels); RL fine-tuning with rule-based rewards in randomly generated sim environments; no primitive-specific demos
setting.observation: Object-centric: humans as predicted constant-velocity future trajectories, regions as rectangle corners, goal position (2D abstraction; on the real robot from ZED tracking + LiDAR + ENML localization)
setting.action_space: Predicted time-dependent 2D waypoint trajectories tracked by MPPI (differential drive)
setting.simulator: Custom 2D simulation (20x20 m arena) + real world
setting.privileged: Ground-truth entities/observations and instruction-to-specification decomposition in simulation (ground-truth annotations were also given to BehAV); rule-based success checks

results: ComposableNav outperforms VLM-Social-Nav, CoNVOI (GPT-4.1) and BehAV at every complexity level. With 3 specifications it reaches 58.6% SR and with 4 specifications 34.9%, while all baselines stay below 11%. RL-fine-tuned primitives reach ~100% versus 27-48% for the pretrained model on most primitives. The system runs in real time on the Jackal robot (replan 0.06 s with 4 primitives).
limitations: Only six primitives with hand-crafted rule-based rewards; this does not scale, and VLM verifiers are left as future work.
Instruction parsing and perception are abstracted away (ground-truth specifications and entities in simulation), so the full pipeline is not closed-loop with an LLM/VLM.
Success rate still drops notably as specifications increase (34.9% at four) because of the naive noise-summing composition; real-world failures come from human tracking loss and jerky replanning.
